items.title: COVID-19 Mythbusters: Fact or Fiction
items.snippet_en: The WHO states there is no scientific evidence that lemon or home remedies prevent or cure COVID-19, nor does drinking water flush out or kill the virus.

items.publisher: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
items.title: Lemon juice will not prevent or cure a COVID-19 infection, no matter what is mixed with it
items.snippet_en: The advisory clarifies that acidic drinks such as lemon juice do not destroy the novel coronavirus inside human cells, and drinking hot lemon juice does not cure or stop infection.

items.title: False claims that drinking water with lemon can prevent COVID-19 circulate online
items.snippet_en: Medical experts confirmed that claims suggesting hot or lukewarm water mixed with lemon can prevent or kill the virus are false, providing no therapeutic effect against SARS-CoV-2.

items.title: Lemon Juice Tea Does Not Cure COVID-19 in Israel, or Anywhere Else
items.snippet_en: Infectious disease specialists confirmed there is no clinical evidence or data showing that lemon juice or hot beverages kill coronavirus in the body.

items.title: Can Lemon And Hot Water Kill Coronavirus? Experts Bust Popular Myths
items.snippet_en: The report highlights official fact-checks clarifying that viral claims stating hot water mixed with lemon kills or eliminates COVID-19 are fake and lack scientific backing.

items.title: No, Vitamin C and lemon-infused hot water do not protect against coronavirus or cancer
items.snippet_en: A fact-check of viral claims found no scientific evidence to support assertions that warm or hot water infused with lemon destroys the coronavirus.

outputs.notes_en: Multiple health organizations, medical experts, and fact-checking outlets have refuted the claim that hot water with lemon juice kills or prevents the coronavirus.
